title: Driverless Taxis Are Coming to European Cities
paragraphs: Driverless taxis are already common in some cities in the United States and China. Now, they are starting to arrive in Europe.

In early September 2026, the ride-hailing company Uber and the British technology company Wayve started a robotaxi service in London. At first, there are fewer than 20 cars. The cars are electric Ford Mustang Mach-E vehicles with Wayve's self-driving technology. Wayve is a British start-up that has received large investments from companies including SoftBank and Uber.

However, a person still sits behind the wheel during each trip. This person can take control of the car if needed. To drive without a person inside, the companies need permission from the UK government, and it is not clear when this will happen.
The robotaxi rides cost the same as normal Uber rides. Passengers cannot choose a robotaxi. Instead, the Uber app may give them one, and they can accept it or say no.

London is not the only European city with robotaxis. In August 2026, Uber started its first commercial robotaxi service in Europe in Zagreb, the capital of Croatia. It works with a local company and the Chinese company Pony.ai. People also sit in the driver's seat there.

Other companies want to come to London too. The American company Waymo, which already runs driverless taxis in 14 US cities, and the Chinese company Baidu are both preparing to start services in London.
But driving in London is not easy. For example, it is not illegal for people to cross the road anywhere they like, which can be difficult for robotaxis.
